import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset from the string
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the bubble chart (a scatter plot with variable size and color)
# This allows us to visualize multiple dimensions:
# x-axis: price_usd
# y-axis: megapixels
# bubble size: max_iso (a measure of light sensitivity)
# bubble color: brand
# marker style: body_type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    size='max_iso',
    hue='brand',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(300, 3000),  # Define the range of bubble sizes for better visual impact
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# Add annotations to each point for more context
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(
        row['price_usd'],
        row['megapixels'],
        f"  {row['model_year']}\n  {row['weight_grams']}g",
        ha='left',
        va='center',
        fontsize=10,
        color='black',
        fontweight='medium'
    )

# Set informative titles and labels
ax.set_title('Camera Feature Comparison: Price vs. Performance', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format x-axis labels to be more readable (e.g., $1,000)
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%1.0f')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Improve readability of the legend
h, l = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate legends for clarity. We find the start of the 'size' legend.
size_legend_start_index = l.index('max_iso')
# Create a legend for hue (brand) and style (body_type)
legend1 = ax.legend(
    handles=h[:size_legend_start_index],
    labels=l[:size_legend_start_index],
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    title='Brand & Body Type',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11'
)
ax.add_artist(legend1) # Re-add the first legend to the plot

# Create a separate legend for size (max_iso)
legend2 = ax.legend(
    handles=h[size_legend_start_index:],
    labels=l[size_legend_start_index:],
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6),
    loc='upper left',
    title='Max ISO',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11'
)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the resulting plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
